run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T15:35:14Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is produced by 15-second Envoy response-timeout 504s on ingress spans, first rising at 15:35:14 (the alert start) and continuing through the end of the window. The specific failing paths are GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout, while GET /, GET /api/data, GET /api/cart and POST /api/cart keep returning 200 in milliseconds. Every failing path converges on ProductCatalogService calls: checkout's own client span to oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct ran 20.0s and 37.5s and ended with gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer' (100.64.188.136 is the product-catalog Service), and checkout failed PlaceOrder with 13 INTERNAL 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product'. The product-catalog service stopped completing work: its GetProduct span completions fell from ~9390 per 900s to 96 and ListProducts to 0, recommendation's calls to product-catalog fell 754 -> 475 -> 219 -> 0, and no GetProduct span completed in 15:40-15:45 (histogram_quantile returned NaN) even though its p90 latency was unchanged at 1.8ms at 15:20 and 15:35. Its pod stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, correct endpoint (100.96.4.247) and no OOM or memory-limit failures, and its CPU fell to near idle (13.6m of a 15m limit at 15:30, 1.6m at 15:40, 0.7m at 15:45) after being CFS-throttled ~2.2-2.5 periods/s while the load ramped. What is firmly supported is where the fault sits (product-catalog stops serving ProductCatalogService traffic, and everything else is downstream of that); why its process stops serving (CPU-limit starvation versus blocking on some external I/O versus another freeze) is not decided by the available evidence, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR rise from ~4-7 per 900s (background, present from 15:14) to 144.8 at 15:35:14, then 273, 413, 546 ... ~1400 by 15:48, while ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET span counts fall from ~10000 to ~900; the 1.42 errors/s in the alert matches ~1400 error spans per 900s.

The errored frontend-proxy ingress spans are HTTP 504 with error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of ~15,000,000 us (15s); each has a child 'router frontend egress' client span of the same ~15s with status_tags error="true" and http.status_code="0" (no response from the frontend).

frontend-proxy access logs name the mechanism and the affected paths: lines such as 'GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 14999' and 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z ... 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000', and in the same period 'GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 - via_upstream ... 26', 'GET /api/data?contextKeys=travel ... 200 ... 3' and 'POST /api/cart ... 200 ... 5'.

The 504 burst is already present in the proxy log at 15:35:48-15:35:59, matching the alert start of 15:35:14, and covers GET /api/products/{id} for several product ids (2ZYFJ3GM2N, L9ECAV7KIM, 6E92ZMYYFZ, OLJCESPC7Z, 0PUK6V6EV0, 9SIQT8TOJO, LS4PSXUNUM), GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout.

In a full trace the chain is load-generator GET (504, 15.0s) -> frontend-proxy ingress (504, 15.0s) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (15.0s, error) -> frontend server span 'GET' (15,000,255us, http.status_code 200) with no child spans; the same trace's later POST /api/cart succeeds end-to-end, so the frontend can still serve other routes during the incident.

The failing dependency is product-catalog: checkout's client span 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' lasted 20,000,730us and 37,504,947us with error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_description 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer'; the parent PlaceOrder span failed with 13 INTERNAL 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"0PUK6V6EV0"' / '#"1YMWWN1N4O"', and frontend POST /api/checkout returned 500.

100.64.188.136 is the product-catalog Service ClusterIP (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080) and its Endpoints object points at the live pod IP 100.96.4.247 (product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9), so the reset came from the product-catalog side, not from a service with no endpoints.

product-catalog stopped completing calls: its completed span counts fall from 9390 (GetProduct) and 766 (ListProducts) per 900s at 15:30 to 96 and 0 at 15:50, and recommendation's own '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts', 'get_product_list' and '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' completions fall 754 -> 475 -> 219 -> 0 over the same period.

The product-catalog server-side latency of the calls it did complete did not degrade: histogram_quantile(0.9) of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket for product-catalog span 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' was 1.82ms at 15:20:14 and 1.83ms at 15:35:14, and returned NaN at 15:45:14 because no GetProduct span completed between 15:40 and 15:45. The stall therefore manifests as requests that never complete, not as slow completions.

In the 10 minutes to 15:49:14 the only spans longer than 10s belong to frontend-proxy (ingress 615.2, router frontend egress 614.1), frontend (GET 565.3, POST 48.4, POST /api/checkout 53.0, executing api route /api/checkout 53.4, grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 61.5), checkout (PlaceOrder 8.1, prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart 61.5, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 16.3) and accounting (order-consumed 2.3); product-catalog, cart, ad, recommendation, payment, currency, email, shipping, quote and image-provider had none.

Error spans by service over the same window show only frontend-proxy (5 -> 273 -> 824 -> 1386 -> 1426 -> 1167 per 900s) and frontend (0 -> 112.8 -> 287.6 -> 295.8 -> 300.2) with a material increase; ad, fraud-detection and recommendation stay at roughly 1 span per 900s and accounting, cart and payment have none.

The product-catalog pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (container started 15:57? no - startedAt 2026-11-16T14:57:26Z), its Deployment reports 1 ready replica, and its container has cpu limit 15m / request 7m, memory limit 30Mi, GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB, PRODUCT_CATALOG_RELOAD_INTERVAL=10 and no liveness or readiness probe.

product-catalog CPU ran at its limit while the load ramped: rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total) was 0.0146 cores at 15:25, 0.0136 at 15:30 against a 15m limit, with CFS throttling rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) of 2.36, 2.33, 2.53 and 2.23 throttled periods/s at 15:15, 15:20, 15:25 and 15:30; after the stall its CPU fell to 0.0016 (15:40) and 0.0007 (15:45) and throttling to 0.16 and 0.03.

There is no memory-limit failure on product-catalog: container_memory_failcnt is 0 for every otel-demo pod across 15:10-15:45, and product-catalog working set stayed at ~25-27MB under its 30Mi limit (page-fault rate fell from ~17-24/s at 15:15-15:30 to 1.3/s at 15:45), so no OOM kill or memory-limit reclaim explains the stall.

product-catalog's application log shows normal work ('Product Found', 'Reloading Product Catalog...' / 'Loaded 10 products' every 10s) through 15:40:27 and nothing later; however log capture for other pods on the same node also ends at ~15:41:35 (cart read_through 15:41:35, frontend-proxy 15:41:34, load-generator 15:41:34), so the missing later product-catalog lines are partly a log-pipeline limitation and are not proof of a frozen process.

The Kubernetes event stream in otel-demo for 15:29:29-15:41:13 contains only fraud-detection container Started/Created/Pulled events at 15:29:29 and periodic product-catalog pod 'Updated' events; no Evicted, OOM, FailedScheduling or probe-failure events appear for product-catalog.

Primary hypothesis: product-catalog's 15m CPU limit (request 7m) cannot serve the ~10-11 req/s ProductCatalogService load that the demo reached at ~15:31 (CPU pinned at its limit and 2.2-2.5 throttled CFS periods/s), the server stops making progress on its queue and clients wait past the proxy's 15s route timeout; the observed near-idle CPU after 15:40 means the throttling alone does not fully explain the final zero-completion state.

Alternative hypothesis: product-catalog's process is blocked on an external I/O dependency (its flagd gRPC endpoint, its OTLP exporter or its stdout/log pipe) rather than CPU-starved, which would explain the combination of zero completions, near-idle CPU (0.0007 cores at 15:45) and no OOM/restart; the available evidence does not show product-catalog's flagd or exporter calls, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Rejected: a flagd outage or a flag-injection fault as the common cause. Cart keeps evaluating flags successfully throughout the incident ('flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' still 552.4 per 900s at 15:35, 405.5 at 15:40, 212.0 at 15:45, 60.7 at 15:50), and the current flagd-config ConfigMap has every flag at defaultVariant 'off'. Whether a flag was in a different state earlier cannot be verified (no change history).

Rejected as primary cause: frontend CPU saturation (limit 100m, usage 0.083-0.088 cores at 15:15-15:30, ~4.0 CFS throttled periods/s, memory rising 251MB -> 341MB at 15:40). During the same window the frontend returned 200 in 3-26ms for GET /, GET /api/data, GET /api/cart and POST /api/cart, its throttling predates the alert, and the independent checkout service hit the same product-catalog resets, so frontend pressure is not the origin.

Rejected: a frontend-proxy defect. The proxy turns slow upstream responses into 504 by design ('504 UT response_timeout' with upstream time 14999-15002ms, i.e. its 15s route timeout) and its own usage is small (0.020-0.024 cores at 15:15-15:30, 0.61-0.75 throttled periods/s against a 30m limit); its ingress span errors start only after the frontend/product-catalog path stalls.

Changed during the window for another reason: fraud-detection restarted at 15:29:29 (restartCount 2) after its previous container terminated with exitCode 137 and reason OOMKilled at 15:29:28, before the alert fired; its own error spans stay at ~1 per 900s and checkout's failures name product-catalog GetProduct, not fraud-detection, so it is not this cause.

Checked and found healthy (no evidence of this failure): cart had 0 error spans and its server spans stayed in the sub-millisecond to ~0.8s range (POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 100-386ms, GetCart 0.4-1.2ms) with normal 'AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync' logs; ad kept ~1 error span per 900s (same as before the alert) and no spans over 10s; currency, payment, email, shipping, quote and accounting had 0 error spans and no spans over 10s (accounting exception noted in gaps); image-provider spans were HTTP 200 with 0us duration; all 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False (state at query time, not during the window).

Add or fix a readiness probe on the product-catalog container and investigate its 15m CPU limit / 7m request and GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB against the observed ~10 req/s load; capture a goroutine/CPU profile or exec into the pod during a recurrence (the pod reported Ready the whole time, so Kubernetes never removed it from the Service).

Investigate why product-catalog's stdout logging stops at 15:40:27 while other pods on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10 keep logging until ~15:41:35, and check the node's log/disk pipeline, so a future stall is distinguishable from a log-collection gap.

gaps: No change history integration is available, so no deployment, image, ConfigMap/resource change before or during the window can be verified; the flagd-config and Deployment resource values quoted are the state at query time and may not equal what ran at 15:35.

The internal reason product-catalog stops serving is unresolved: the evidence shows zero completions and near-idle CPU but cannot distinguish CPU-limit starvation from blocking on an external dependency or a process-level freeze; no goroutine dump, CPU profile, or container-level process diagnostics were available.

product-catalog container logs end at 15:40:27 and log capture for the pods on that node ends ~15:41:35, so the absence of later log lines is not evidence of a freeze; the frontend and recommendation containers returned no log lines at all in the window.
No data exists past 2026-11-16T15:50:28Z, so whether product-catalog recovered or the error rate is still elevated is unknown.
accounting had 2.3 spans over 10s on 'order-consumed' in the last 10 minutes that are not explained or tied to this cause; its internal state was not checked.
The frontend container's memory working set rose from ~253MB to ~346MB at 15:40-15:45 while its Deployment declares a 200Mi limit; the reason for that level/delta and its effect were not determined.
next_steps: During a recurrence, capture a goroutine dump / SIGQUIT stack trace from the product-catalog container and check whether it is blocked on flagd, the OTLP exporter, or stdout writes.

Review product-catalog resource settings (cpu limit 15m, request 7m, GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB in a 30Mi container) versus the ~10-11 req/s load and consider raising them; verify CFS throttling history for that pod at finer than 5-minute resolution.
Add a readiness probe to product-catalog so Kubernetes stops routing to it when it stops serving, since it stayed Ready with 0 restarts throughout.
Check node i-0b2137ceca968ac10 log/disk pipeline health around 15:40-15:42 to separate a log-collection gap from an application stall.
